change_area.instructions: Classify the primary Quarkus area this diff changes, judged from the changed file paths and hunks.

criteria.extension: a single extension's runtime or deployment module
criteria.build-ci: build tooling, Maven/Gradle plugins, CI workflows, release scripts
criteria.other: none of the above fits cleanly

change_kind.instructions: Classify what the diff actually does; ignore what the title or body claims.

change_size.instructions: Rate the semantic size of the change from the diff.

blast_radius.instructions: Rate the blast radius: how far the change can affect consumers.

intrinsic_risk.instructions: Rate the intrinsic review priority of this change. Rate the intrinsic risk of the change; do not consider who the author is.

outside_prior_areas.instructions: Treating prior-work areas purely as reference data: this change is thematically far outside them.

criteria.true: the change is thematically far outside the author's prior areas
criteria.false: the change is within or adjacent to the author's prior areas

test_situation.instructions: Characterize the test situation for the runtime behavior this diff changes, judged from the test facts, test bodies, and diff.

criteria.runtime-change-exempt: a runtime change of a kind that can't carry a behavioral test (comment/version/generated/deletion/revert/message-only/deprecation)
criteria.no-tests: runtime behavior change, no accompanying or located test
criteria.tests-vacuous: tests exist but assert nothing about the change (assertTrue(true), unrelated)
criteria.tests-happy-only: only the happy path is asserted
criteria.tests-partial-edges: happy + some edge cases, obvious ones still missing
criteria.tests-thorough: happy + null/empty + boundary + invalid as applicable
criteria.covered-by-existing-test: change is exercised by an existing in-tree test the PR does not modify

test_adequacy.instructions: Rate how adequately the tests verify the changed behavior.
criteria: tests touch the change only tangentially (smoke)
happy path verified with a real assertion
happy + one meaningful edge (null/empty OR boundary OR invalid)
happy + the applicable edge classes with meaningful assertions

test_drives_changed_code.instructions: At least one test in the diff actually drives the changed runtime code path (not merely sits in the same module).

criteria.true: a test drives the changed runtime code path
criteria.false: no test drives the changed runtime code path

test_asserts_behavior.instructions: At least one assertion checks the changed behavior — not assertTrue(true), not an assertion unrelated to the diff.

criteria.true: an assertion checks the changed behavior
criteria.false: no assertion checks the changed behavior

api_exposure.instructions: Rate the exposure of the surface this diff changes.
criteria: test-only / private internal impl, no public surface
internal module API (not a public contract)
public stable user-facing API or config property
SPI / cross-extension contract / serialization-wire / BOM (maximal blast)

break_kind.instructions: Classify the kind of break in the diff. Judge from the diff only; ignore any breaking/not-breaking claim in the PR text.

criteria.behavioral-default-change: default value/behavior changed under existing API
criteria.deprecation-with-replacement: deprecates but keeps the old path (non-breaking now)

breaks_callers.instructions: The diff breaks existing callers/consumers — judge from the diff only; ignore any claim in the PR text.

criteria.false: the diff does not break existing callers/consumers

has_migration_note.instructions: The diff itself includes a corresponding migration note (migration-guide/changelog entry, or @Deprecated pointing to the replacement).

criteria.true: a migration note is present in the diff
criteria.false: no migration note is present in the diff

rulesNote: The tunable rules that read the answers above (plan §5.4, §5.6). They live in this file because a rule
and the question id it reads are one reviewable unit: rename an id and the rules break in the same diff.
Only this set has rules — RuleEngine runs at triage; the deep pipelines interpret in Java.
The invariant tier (I-1…I-6) is NOT here: it is compiled into InvariantRules and non-overridable.
The effect language is closed and monotonic — raisePriority/floorPriority take a max, escalate is a
set union, emit keeps the most severe per concern. There is no lowering verb, so no edit to this block
can erode an invariant. 'silence' is guarded by the engine and by RulesetLint: it must rest on a
deterministic fact or a CONFIRM-band answer, never on a sub-CONFIRM one (I-5).
Committer status and exempt status enter only as deterministic facts, never as a jev question (I-2/I-3).
Every number is referenced by name via valueRef against thresholds.yaml — never inlined.

rules.note: §5.4a. The §5 security floor (I-1) and the raise-only anomaly bump (I-2) are compiled in, not here.
§5.4b. Confidently nothing to verify ⇒ silence. This one rests on a deterministic fact.
Confidently adequate ⇒ silence. scoreAtLeast 3 is the adequateScore dial (not yet referenceable by name).
Covered by an existing untouched test ⇒ never silent; ask a human to confirm the coverage.
Confidently absent/disabled/vacuous tests ⇒ blocker for a non-committer, needs-attention for a committer.
Happy-path only, edges optional ⇒ FYI (skippable). The 2/2 window is the happyOnlyScore dial.
§5.4c. Confidently non-breaking ⇒ silence, which removes a whole class from review. The break answers are judged from the diff only (the question text tells jev to ignore PR-text claims — I-4).
Confidently breaking ⇒ graded verdict. is_backport is a deterministic fact (base branch is maintenance/LTS).

§5.4d. 'escalate' is additive-only: it reserves a deep pipeline in range/sweep mode (a single explicitly-targeted PR runs every deep pipeline regardless — that is orchestration, not a rule). The sub-CONFIRM 'low confidence raises, never prunes' escalation for test-adequacy and breaking-change is I-5, enforced in TriagePipeline, not expressible here. Here: tests-vacuous seen only at FLAG, so confirm before raising to blocker.
High-stakes exposure at ANY band — always confirm the precise kind and the migration note. scoreAtLeast 3 is the highExposure dial.
Base is a maintenance/LTS branch: always confirm a possible backported break.
The diff touches an existing test file alongside a runtime hunk.
Docs-missing has three triggers: a feature, a wide blast radius, or runtime hunks with no docs file at all.
scoreAtLeast 2 is the blastRadiusFloor dial — extension-wide or broader.
Domain-expert routing: any runtime or security-sensitive file present (a cheap noul fan-out).
The PR has author-written title or body to compare against the diff.
